points: The Most High asks where is the bill of the mother's divorcement, or which creditor he sold them to. The point of the charge is that for their iniquities they sold themselves, and for their transgressions their mother was put away.
This is not that the people literally went and sold themselves. They brought this upon themselves by their own sins, and that is what put them into their trouble.

points: His hand is not shortened that it cannot redeem, and he has power to deliver. At his rebuke he dries up the sea, makes the rivers a wilderness, and clothes the heavens with blackness.

note.label: Isaiah 50: The Servant's Obedience and the Prophecy of Christ Beaten

points: The Lord God gave the Servant the tongue of the learned, to know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary, and he wakens the ear morning by morning to hear as the learned.

note.label: Isaiah 50: The Servant's Obedience and the Prophecy of Christ Beaten

points: The Servant was not rebellious and did not turn away back. He gave his back to the smiters and his cheeks to them that plucked off the hair, and he hid not his face from shame and spitting.
This goes right into the prophecy of Christ, who was getting beat. The gave-my-back-to-the-smiters is the beating and shame he took.

note.label: Isaiah 50: The Servant's Obedience and the Prophecy of Christ Beaten

points: Because the Lord God will help him, the Servant is not confounded; he sets his face like a flint and knows he shall not be ashamed. The one who justifies him is near, so who will contend with him or condemn him.

note.label: Isaiah 50: The Servant's Obedience and the Prophecy of Christ Beaten

points: His adversaries shall wax old as a garment and the moth shall eat them up. The one who fears the Lord and obeys the voice of his servant, though he walks in darkness and has no light, is told to trust in the name of the Lord and stay upon his God.

note.label: Isaiah 50: The Servant's Obedience and the Prophecy of Christ Beaten

points: Those who kindle their own fire and compass themselves with sparks, walking in the light of their own fire, shall have this at his hand: they shall lie down in sorrow.
